learningObjective: Enumerate factors that make a static analytical cost model differ from measured wall-clock runtime.

canonicalClaims.claim: Static analytical cost models built on op counts and shape arithmetic systematically diverge from measured runtime because they omit backend register allocation / spill decisions, cache and TLB context effects, and low-level hardware phenomena such as bank conflicts and memory-controller queuing.
conditions: The cost model is built solely from source-level features (op counts, tensor shapes).
Measurements are taken after standard warmup and averaging.
nonImplications: Does not imply analytical models are useless; they effectively prune the search space.
Does not imply learned models fully close the gap.

misconceptions.claim: Once warmup is complete, the cost model equals the measurement, so no gap exists.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Even after warmup, backend spills, cache context, and hardware queuing remain outside a source-level analytical model.

misconceptions.claim: Cost-model divergence is caused by JIT-warmup effects and disappears once the first N runs are discarded.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Warmup is a measurement-methodology issue, not a source of model-vs-measurement divergence.

misconceptions.claim: Analytical cost models can be made exact if built on the same precision as the hardware.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Numerical precision of the model has no bearing on missing modelling of backend and hardware effects.

misconceptions.claim: Measurement-based ranking is inherently unreliable due to noise; static cost models are strictly more trustworthy.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Well-designed measurement (multiple runs, median) is more accurate than analytical cost for real hardware; static models are cheaper but less accurate.

implementationFacts: Ansor trains an XGBoost / MLP cost model on measured runtimes to guide the search.
MetaSchedule (in TVM) similarly uses a learned cost model over TensorIR features.
AutoTVM uses measurement-based ranking with a trained proposal model.
performanceScenarios: For GEMM tiles, a purely FLOPs+bytes model may rank a spill-inducing candidate optimistically; measurement re-ranks it.
